## Rio Carnival and Iguazu Falls in eight days

This itinerary has two main aims: to watch the samba-school parade at the Sambadrome and visit [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) from both sides of the border. **Eight days and seven nights** are divided between [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Foz do Iguaçu. There is no separate Amazon segment or series of beach resorts: the route remains focused on Carnival and the waterfalls.

The group departure dates are **February 5–12**, with no year specified. In 2027, official main-group parades take place on **February 7–9**. When selecting the trip, align the actual departure year, Sambadrome ticket date, and daily itinerary to ensure the Carnival event takes place on the evening covered by your ticket.

## The eight-day itinerary

| Day | Main plan |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival in Rio |
| 2 | Sugarloaf Mountain and the old city |
| 3 | Free time and the Sambadrome |
| 4 | Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer |
| 5 | Flight to Iguazu |
| 6 | Brazilian side of the falls |
| 7 | Argentine side of the falls |
| 8 | Departure |

Travelers spend **the first four nights** in Rio. Sugarloaf Mountain offers panoramic views of Guanabara Bay, the city beaches, and the surrounding mountains. A tour of the old center reveals another side of the city: churches, the cathedral, and historic buildings. Then comes Carnival night at the Sambadrome, followed on the next day by Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue.

Carnival occupies a dedicated evening, with free daytime hours scheduled beforehand. This matters because the nighttime parade may end late; it should not be treated like an ordinary four-hour daytime excursion.

**The next three nights** are spent in the Iguazu area. After flying from Rio, travelers first visit the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. The following day is devoted to the Argentine side, with walkways reaching closer to the cascades. Changing countries means crossing a national border, even though the tour's primary geography remains Brazil.

## How the two sides of the falls differ

From Brazil, you can see the long line of cascades and the great forested canyon. This provides a broad view of the entire natural complex. On the Argentine side, trails and walkways bring visitors nearer individual streams for a closer look at the moving water.

The itinerary allocates a separate day to each side, so you do not need to choose which one is “better.” The excursions complement each other, offering different experiences of the same natural wonder.

## Carnival tickets and included services

The price includes accommodation in selected hotels with breakfast, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, transfers, Carnival tickets, and transportation between the hotel and the Sambadrome in both directions. Attending the celebration is therefore part of the paid itinerary, not an optional free evening.

**The Rio–Iguazu flight is paid for separately**, with an indicative cost **from $250**. International flights, optional excursions, and meals and drinks during transfers are also excluded. The stated program price is **$2981**; compare rates with all separately charged items in mind.

The eight days are quite tightly scheduled. There is less time for independent relaxation by the ocean than on an ordinary week-long Rio holiday. In return, travelers combine a major urban event with a natural attraction for which other itineraries devote a separate trip.

## How this differs from other Carnival tours

The [12-day Carnival itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-amazon-buzios/) adds the Amazon and Búzios beaches. It suits travelers who want to cover more regions and are prepared for additional flights.

The [private premium Rio–Iguazu itinerary](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-8-days/) features other accommodation and service options, a helicopter excursion, and a private boat. An important distinction is that the actual Carnival events and current dates need to be checked for the particular product: a similar duration does not mean the same tickets.

Explore all available options under [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [events and festivals trips](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/).

## Frequently asked questions about Carnival and Iguazu

### How many nights are spent in Rio?

Four nights. City excursions, free daytime hours, and an evening celebration at the Sambadrome are scheduled there.

### Are samba-parade tickets included?

Yes. Carnival admission tickets and transfers to and from the Sambadrome are among the included services.

### Does the itinerary visit the Argentine side of Iguazu?

Yes. Day 7 is dedicated to the Argentine waterfalls.

### Is the flight between Rio and Iguazu included?

No. It is paid for separately, with an indicative cost from $250.

### Does the program include the Amazon?

No. To include the Amazon and the beaches of Búzios, choose the longer Carnival itinerary.

## Rio Carnival, Iguazu, the Amazon, and Búzios in 12 days

This itinerary is designed for travelers who want to combine **Rio Carnival** with several of Brazil's major natural regions. Over **12 days**, it passes through [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the Amazon rainforest, and the beaches of [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). Flights connect the principal excursion segments, while the final day on the coast is free.

Group departure dates are **February 5–16**, with no year specified in the record itself. Carnival dates must be aligned with a particular season: for example, the official 2027 calendar schedules main-group samba-school performances for **February 7–9**. Choose this tour with the actual Sambadrome visit and valid tickets in mind, before focusing on the overall number of days.

## How the days and nights are divided

| Days | Main destination |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio, excursions, and Carnival |
| 5–7 | Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu |
| 8–9 | The Amazon and a river program |
| 10–11 | Búzios and beach relaxation |
| 12 | Return to Rio airport |

**Rio: four nights.** Following arrival, travelers gradually discover the city. Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, and historic neighborhoods are scheduled on different days. On Day 3, the centerpiece is a visit to the Sambadrome, where samba schools perform with music, costumes, and moving floats. Carnival admission and round-trip hotel–Sambadrome transfers are listed among the included services.

**Iguazu: three nights.** After flying from Rio, the first excursion is on the Brazilian side, with broad panoramas of the falls. On the next day, the itinerary continues on the Argentine side. Trails and walkways provide close-up views of the cascades; this is a separate cross-border visit, although Brazil is the tour's main country.

**The Amazon: two nights.** After traveling via Manaus, visitors explore the river and forest. The program includes a guided forest walk, traditional activities, and evening wildlife observation. Additional dolphin encounters and other activities should be distinguished from what is mandatory.

**Búzios: two nights.** The final stage takes place on the tropical coast. After a busy journey, there is time for the beach and unhurried walks. Day 12 is allocated to the return via Rio.

## The Sambadrome: what is included

Carnival is **a central event in this itinerary**, not merely a chance to happen upon festivities in the city. The price includes Carnival admission and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers. The exact ticket type and parade date must match the confirmed departure and ticket.

The official Carnival program changes from year to year. In 2027, the main-group parades are scheduled for **February 7, 8, and 9**, with the Champions' Parade on **February 13**. These are different events; when comparing Carnival tours, check precisely which evening your ticket covers.

Rio has much to offer outside Carnival. Excursions to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain reveal the bays, mountains, and beaches, while the historic center allows time for architecture rather than spending every day at the festival venue.

## What the tour includes and how much flights cost

Accommodation with breakfast in selected hotels, scheduled excursions, transfers, and Carnival tickets are included. Main excursions use a **Russian-speaking guide**; in Manaus, services are provided by an **English-speaking guide**.

**Domestic flights are not included.** The indicative cost of the Rio–Iguazu–Manaus–Rio flights starts **from $850**. International tickets, optional excursions, and meals and drinks during transfers are also paid for separately. The program price is **$4806**; account for flights and the actual group composition when comparing it with other trips.

There is an alternative to the final beach days: instead of Búzios, you can choose [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/) with all-inclusive accommodation. However, this option requires a minimum of **three nights**, whereas the base itinerary finishes with two nights in Búzios. Such a change must therefore be agreed as an adjustment to dates and cost, rather than assumed to be equivalent.

## Who the 12-day program suits

This tour works well for guests for whom Carnival is an important objective, but who also want to use a long flight to Brazil to experience its natural attractions. After the parade, the journey continues to the falls and the Amazon before ending with a coastal holiday.

If Carnival and the falls are enough, consider the [eight-day Rio–Iguazu itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-8-days/). Travelers mainly interested in city sightseeing without fixed festive dates may prefer the [week-long Rio program](/brazil/tour/best-of-rio-de-janeiro/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 12-day Carnival tour

### Are Sambadrome tickets included?

Yes. The paid services include Carnival tickets and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers.

### Are both sides of Iguazu visited?

Yes. Separate excursion days cover the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls.

### Is the guide Russian-speaking throughout?

Russian-language guiding is specified for the main excursions; an English-speaking guide is provided in Manaus.

### Can Búzios be replaced with Angra dos Reis?

This option is offered, but accommodation in Angra dos Reis requires at least three nights. The length and terms of the base tour must be adjusted separately.

### Are flights within Brazil included?

No. The indicative cost of the Rio–Iguazu–Manaus–Rio segments starts from $850.

## Rio, Iguazu, Pantanal, and Búzios in 12 days: how the journey unfolds

This [Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/) has four main stops, each offering something different. The first days focus on Rio's urban panoramas, followed by waterfalls, wildlife observation on a vast wetland plain, and relaxation beside the ocean. The duration is **12 days and 11 nights**. Each region offers a distinct experience, so simply listing the destinations does not convey the entire program.

| Region | Nights |
|---|---:|
| [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) | 3 |
| [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) | 2 |
| [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) | 3 |
| [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/) | 3 |

In practice, the itinerary also includes several days involving airports and transfers. This order suits travelers who want to leave the beach segment until the end, after city sightseeing and active nature excursions.

## What happens at each stage of the journey

**Rio de Janeiro, Days 1–3.** On arrival, travelers transfer to their hotel. The main sightseeing days include Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado with the Christ the Redeemer statue. These viewpoints show the coast, bay, and city from different directions. A tour of the historic center adds old Rio's architecture and streets to the panoramas.

**Iguazu, Days 4–5.** After a domestic flight, the group arrives in Foz do Iguaçu. The main excursion explores the Brazilian side of the national park, overlooking the system of waterfalls. The Bird Park and a “Macuco Safari” boat trip are available as optional extras and should not be assumed to be included in the base rate. If you want to see the Argentine side, arrange a separate visit and check the documents required for the border crossing.

**Pantanal, Days 6–8.** The flight to Campo Grande is followed by a road transfer. Activities during the nature portion focus on bird- and wildlife-watching, including a horseback ride and other activities specified in the itinerary. The environment itself is the attraction: waterways and pools, bird-filled banks, caimans, and open spaces. Animals move freely, so the excursions provide opportunities to watch them but cannot guarantee a sighting of any specific species.

**Búzios, Days 9–11.** After flying back to Rio, travelers transfer to the oceanfront peninsula. Several free days allow you to choose beaches with different surf conditions or additional sea activities. Boat trips and other activities may be available, but check the final program's inclusions: not everything mentioned is automatically part of the price.

Day 12 includes a private transfer via Rio to the international airport. This is an important logistical stage, especially for an early flight.

## Why the Pantanal requires separate planning

The [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) is a seasonally flooded plain, with conditions on waterways and for wildlife observation changing as water levels rise and fall. When choosing dates, consider what matters most: birdwatching and overland outings, boat excursions, or a combination. One generic “best season for Brazil” is insufficient: in Rio and Búzios you spend time by the ocean, while in the Pantanal, conditions in the natural environment shape the outcome of the visit.

The word “safari” should not be taken as a promise of jaguar sightings or encounters with other rare animals. Seeing particular species requires suitable areas, conditions, seasons, and dedicated routes that cannot be assumed to be part of the general three-night itinerary.

Compare the time spent in the Pantanal among [Brazil nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) and options where wildlife observation occupies most of the journey.

## Private and shared excursions: what is the difference?

The tour's name may contain the word “private,” but actual arrangements vary across regions. In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Iguazu, **private excursions with Russian-speaking guides** are included. In the Pantanal, **shared excursions with English-speaking guides** are listed among the inclusions. Private transfers by car are provided separately.

This distinction matters when choosing a tour, particularly if you require Russian-language guiding every day or your own guide for every nature outing. Changes can be discussed, but are not presented as standard inclusions.

## Flights, expenses, and travel pace

The itinerary involves domestic flights from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu, then Campo Grande, and back to Rio. **Domestic tickets, international flights, meals and drinks, and optional excursions** are listed as separate costs. Evaluate the travel budget with flights and potential additional activities in mind, rather than only the starting price of the main program.

Traveling across several climate zones calls for flexible packing: light clothes for the coast, sun protection, footwear for wet or uneven nature trails, and a change of clothing after rain. Layers are useful for early-morning safari activities. Confirm the conditions and physical demands of individual excursions when booking.

If your priority is simply beaches and Rio, compare this option with other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/). If wildlife is the main goal, compare [nature and wildlife programs](/interests/wildlife/) by the number of days in the Pantanal rather than total duration alone.

## Frequently asked questions about the Rio–Iguazu–Pantanal–Búzios itinerary

### Are all 12 days accompanied by a private Russian-speaking guide?

No. Rio and Iguazu feature private Russian-language excursions; the Pantanal offers shared excursions in English. Transfers and other services are described separately.

### Are flights between regions included in the main price?

No. Domestic flights are listed among expenses excluded from the base program price.

### Are jaguar or other rare animal sightings guaranteed?

No. Nature activities and opportunities to see wildlife are included, but specific Pantanal encounters are not guaranteed.

### Can I spend more time at the beaches?

The current program allocates three nights to Búzios. Changing the number of days and allocation of stops requires a separately agreed revision of the itinerary.

## Six-day Brazil tour: Rio de Janeiro and both sides of Iguazu Falls

This itinerary lets you experience the famous panoramas of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Iguazu Falls during a short holiday. City excursions include Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado, followed by a flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) to see the falls from the Brazilian side and a separate visit to the [Argentine park](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

**Six days and five nights** are designed for travelers more interested in major natural and city sights than an extended beach holiday. There is no separate resort segment, and Days 4 and 6 involve flights.

## Three days in Rio: what can you see?

Day 1 is allocated to arrival, meeting at the airport, a transfer to the hotel, and rest. If you have enough energy, you can spend the evening walking along the seafront.

On Day 2, the cable car takes visitors via Morro da Urca up Sugarloaf Mountain. From the summit, you can see Guanabara Bay, the city beaches, the Rio–Niterói Bridge, and Corcovado. After descending, a sightseeing tour introduces Rio's colonial architecture and central districts. Visits to the cathedral and a stop at the Selarón Steps are possible, but not guaranteed.

Day 3 is devoted to the journey through Tijuca Forest to Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue. These two heights show different aspects of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/): Sugarloaf is closer to the bay and ocean, while Corcovado affords views over a vast part of the city between the mountains.

## Iguazu: what the Brazilian and Argentine sides offer

After the flight on Day 4, travelers arrive in Foz do Iguaçu. That day you explore the cascades and viewpoints on the [Brazilian side of the falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where much of the waterfall system can be seen at once. A Macuco Safari boat trip and a visit to the Bird Park can be booked as extras; they are not part of the base excursion price.

Day 5 features an excursion to the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) along constructed walkways and aboard an ecological train. This brings visitors closer to the waterfalls, including the area around Devil's Throat. Participants should check entry requirements for Argentina and re-entry into Brazil according to their citizenship.

Because the excursion crosses a national border, the time required for controls depends on how busy the crossings are. Avoid reducing the time allocated to this day when choosing optional activities: the park walks require time and comfortable shoes.

## Time and transfers

| Day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival and hotel check-in in Rio |
| 2 | Sugarloaf Mountain and city |
| 3 | Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer |
| 4 | Rio–Iguazu flight |
| 5 | Argentine side of the falls |
| 6 | Flight back to Rio, onward international connection |

**The Rio–Iguazu–Rio domestic flight is not included**, with an indicative price from $300. When budgeting for the entire trip, account separately for tickets, luggage, and the connection time between the arrival of your domestic flight and your international departure.

Avoid buying separate tickets with a minimum connection on Day 6 without confirming the return flight schedule. If the domestic service is delayed, catching your international flight may become difficult.

## What the itinerary includes

Accommodation in hotels, **shared excursions with a Russian-speaking guide**, and shared driver-operated transfers are included. Optional excursions, domestic flights, and meals and drinks during transfers are paid for separately. Accommodation configuration and international ticket details are confirmed when preparing an individual quotation.

The itinerary works particularly well as a first introduction to Brazil: in a short period, visitors see famous urban landmarks and the falls. Free time for relaxation, however, is limited.

## If you want more nature or beaches

The six-day version is a compact sightseeing itinerary. For a longer ocean holiday after city excursions, consider the [eight-day Rio and Búzios tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-buzios-8-days/). To include the Amazon as well, explore the [Rio, Iguazu, Amazon and Búzios itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-amazon-iguazu-beaches/), which takes much more time and several additional flights.

## Frequently asked questions about the six-day tour

### Can I see Rio and Iguazu in six days?

Yes. The program specifically combines three days in Rio with a flight to the falls and sightseeing on both sides of the border.

### Is the Argentine side of Iguazu included?

Yes. It is scheduled for Day 5. Entry documents for Argentina depend on each traveler's citizenship.

### Is the domestic flight included?

No. The Rio–Iguazu–Rio flights are paid for separately, with an indicative price from $300.

### Is there time for beaches?

You may be able to enjoy an independent walk beside the ocean in Rio, but the program does not include a separate multi-day beach holiday.

### What language are the excursions in?

The main excursions are shared group activities with a Russian-speaking guide.

## How the eight-day Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu Falls tour works

The itinerary combines a city holiday in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with nature excursions to Iguazu. The first days are spent by the ocean, on Sugarloaf Mountain, and at Corcovado. You then head to the falls, where visits to **both the Brazilian and Argentine sides** of the same natural complex are included.

The program lasts **eight days and seven nights**. The first four days are in Rio, Day 5 involves traveling and flying to the Foz do Iguaçu area, Days 6 and 7 focus on the falls, and Day 8 is for the return to the airport.

## Four days in Rio: the core itinerary

After arrival and the hotel transfer, free time remains. **On Day 2**, visitors travel to Praia Vermelha and take the cable car via Morro da Urca to Sugarloaf Mountain. The viewpoints overlook the city and bay.

**Day 3** begins with the historic center: churches, squares, old buildings, and the cathedral. The excursion then continues to Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue. Each of these excursions lasts approximately **four hours**.

**Day 4** can be spent relaxing independently or on optional excursions. Possible choices include [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/), [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/), Rio by night, and other city itineraries. These are not already-paid components of the base program.

## Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu

After the flight, the journey continues near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). **Day 6** is spent on the Brazilian side, famous for broad panoramas of cascades and walkways near the waterfalls.

**Day 7** is devoted to crossing via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) to the Argentine side. Walkways here lead nearer individual streams, offering views of the falls from different directions. This is a compulsory part of the stated itinerary even though the journey as a whole is presented as a Brazil tour.

The two sides are separated by a national border. Check entry and return-crossing rules for the traveler’s citizenship and route. Some park trails may close temporarily because of weather or maintenance.

| Day | Main event |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio, sightseeing and relaxation |
| 5 | Flight to Foz do Iguaçu |
| 6 | Brazilian side |
| 7 | Argentine side |
| 8 | Airport transfer |

## Which services are included and which cost extra?

The program includes hotels with breakfast, private excursions in Rio and Iguazu with a Russian-speaking guide, and private transfers with a driver.

**The domestic flight from Rio to Iguazu is not included**, nor is the international flight. Optional excursions and food and drinks outside the specified package are also paid for separately. The budget should therefore combine the cost of the tour itself, flights, and selected extras, taking into account flight schedules on Days 5 and 8.

When choosing among [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), compare not just the number of days but also the geography of mandatory excursions. The Argentine side of Iguazu is already part of this itinerary, while the extra outings from Rio remain up to each traveler.

## Preparing for the waterfalls

For city sightseeing, bring comfortable shoes, a hat, and sun protection. At Iguazu, non-slip shoes, a waterproof cover for your phone, and dry spare clothes are useful because the viewpoints can be very wet with spray. Walking routes take time, so it is sensible to keep the two sides on separate days.

## Frequently asked questions about the eight-day tour

### Is the Argentine side of Iguazu included?

Yes. A visit to the Argentine waterfalls is scheduled for Day 7 of the main itinerary.

### Is the Rio–Iguazu flight included?

No. Domestic air tickets are explicitly listed among costs outside the tour price.

### Are excursions on the free day already paid for?

No. Trips to Angra dos Reis, Petrópolis, and other destinations on Day 4 are offered as optional extras.
